item.title: Java Testing Strategies to Intercept System Out and System Err
item.description:
“Java Testing Strategies to Intercept System Out and System Err”

Testing code that interacts directly with standard input/output streams (System.out, System.err) presents a challenge because these streams are global to the JVM. Redirecting them during a test requires careful setup and teardown to prevent side effects on other parallel tests or the rest of the application. Several methods exist, ranging from manual stream manipulation to employing specialized testing libraries.

Manual Stream Redirection with Lifecycle Hooks (JUnit 4/5)

A fundamental approach involves temporarily replacing System.out and System.err with PrintStream wrappers connected to a ByteArrayOutputStream before the test execution and restoring the originals afterward. This pattern often utilizes @Before/@BeforeEach for setup and @After/@AfterEach for cleanup.
